a-little-princess-being-the-whole-story-: Burnett's 1905 Little Princess expands Sara Crewe's attic tale to full novel. Imagination triumphs. The Tower library holds the full text. govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PassporttoAssas:
An advertisement promotes 'Passport to Assassination,' a book about Lee Harvey Oswald. Its author is Oleg Maximovich Nechiporenko, a retired colonel of the KGB. The book was translated from the Russian. Nechiporenko had dealt with Oswald in Mexico City, where Oswald visited the Soviet consulate weeks before the assassination.

A KGB officer's memoir of Oswald was a publishing event of the post-Cold War years. The Soviet file on Oswald had been one of the case's locked rooms. The advertisement sells that access: the other side's officer, telling the story in English. It preserves the pitch made to Western readers, and the credential it rested on.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-WheelerBurtonKS: PM, the New York daily, reported a meeting between Senators Burton Wheeler and Gerald Nye and a man named Kamp. Wheeler and Nye were leading isolationists before the Second World War, opposed to American entry into the conflict. Their meetings drew press attention because both men shaped the foreign policy fight of their day. The short article preserves one such encounter as the paper reported it.
govdocs-archive_org-the-great-ufo-hoax-t: Gregory M. Kanon argues the opposite of most UFO books: the whole phenomenon is a deliberate hoax. His 1997 book, The Great UFO Hoax, promises a final solution to the UFO mystery. Kanon treats sightings, stories, and famous cases as parts of a made-up system that serves its makers. Skeptical readers get a full case here, built to explain not just a few sightings but the entire belief.
govdocs-nsarchive-Briefing_Book_foia_FOI:
The world's first freedom of information act dates to 1766, two and a half centuries before this briefing book marked the anniversary in December 2016. Lauren Harper edited the set, number 568. Its hero is Finland's Anders Chydenius, an early champion of open records.

By 2016, freedom of information laws had spread to 113 countries. The posting argues that the United States law still has room to grow if America wants to lead on transparency. The long view is the point: a practice now treated as normal began as a radical idea in eighteenth-century Finland and Sweden.
govdocs-nsarchive-Briefing_Book_mexico_U:
Since 2007 the United States has run its Mexico policy through a small circle of Mexican partner officials, under the Mérida Initiative. This briefing book, posted in December 2020, examines what happened when American prosecutions turned toward that circle. Corruption inside the partnership came into focus.

A wide-ranging aid program built on trusted counterparts faces an obvious risk: what if the counterparts are compromised? Court cases in the United States forced that question into the open. The documents here let readers trace how Washington's chosen partners were vetted, used, and in some cases prosecuted by the same government that had relied on them.
govdocs-nsarchive-Briefing_Book_russia-p:
Anatoly Chernyaev kept a diary while working inside the Soviet leadership, years before he became Mikhail Gorbachev's close aide. In May 2022, the National Security Archive published his diary for 1982 in English for the first time. The date marked what would have been his 101st birthday, and the edition was prepared by Svetlana Savranskaya.

The year 1982 sits in the run-up to perestroika, when Leonid Brezhnev was dying and reform had not yet begun. A diary like this records what a well-placed insider saw, heard, and worried about day by day, rather than what officials later claimed. For readers, it is a ground-level view of a tired system in its last years before change arrived.
govdocs-nsarchive-Briefing_Book_southern: Barack Obama's administration made declassification a tool of diplomacy with Argentina, promising to open American files on the dirty war of 1976 to 1983. A National Security Archive briefing book page carries that policy under the headline of Obama bringing declassified diplomacy to Argentina. The evidence preserved for this entry is the page capture alone, without the release's underlying documents, so it marks the moment and the policy rather than reproducing the records. Its companion postings in the Archive detail the examples of material such an opening could surface.

A court in Rome spent three years trying the cross-border repression that Latin America's military regimes ran together as Operation Condor. Briefing Book number 577, edited by Carlos Osorio and published in January 2017, covers the verdict: life sentences, summed up in the Archive's headline as condemned to life.

The National Security Archive supplied declassified evidence to the tribunal and welcomed the ruling as historic. That role matters here: secret American files, pried loose over years, ended up as proof in an Italian courtroom judging crimes committed in South America decades earlier. For readers, the posting shows the long road evidence travels, from classified vaults to a judge's bench, before justice of any kind becomes possible.
podcast-joerogan-9iENvZ2siTo:
Drummer Travis Barker joins Joe Rogan for episode 2540. Barker powers the pop-punk band Blink-182 with fast, sharp playing. His life off stage has been as loud as his kit.

He survived a deadly plane crash and rebuilt his career after it. Rogan draws out tales of tours, tattoos, and fame. They also touch on his life inside a famous reality family. The episode gives rock fans a rare long sit with a drummer who rarely stops moving, told in his own dry voice. Few drummers have lived a story half as wild.
marx-communist-manifesto:
Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels published The Communist Manifesto in London in February 1848, weeks before revolutions swept Europe. The pamphlet was the program of the Communist League, a small band of exiled workers and thinkers. It runs barely thirty pages, and it changed the world.

The text tells history as a long fight between classes, now between owners and workers. It praises the energy of modern industry, then predicts its owners will dig its grave. Ten demands close the argument, from free schooling to steep income taxes. The call for workers of all lands to unite rings from its last page.
florenz-quellen-shinto:
Karl Florenz published his Shinto sourcebook in German in 1919. The Historical Sources of the Shinto Religion was the first of its kind. Florenz ranked as the finest German Japanologist of his generation.

The Kojiki and the Nihongi supply the book's core ancient texts. Old Norito prayers join them in careful, scholarly German dress. Florenz guides readers through myth, rite, and imperial cult with notes. Students gained a firm path into Japan's native faith from his work. The sourcebook still anchors study of Shinto's oldest written records in the West. Florenz's care with hard texts set a standard for those who followed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-montalto: Montalto, the Calabrian hill town, became a bishop's see serving the rugged interior of the toe of Italy. This entry covers its diocese, its churches, and its history. The faith in the Calabrian hills, where Greek and Latin traditions met for centuries.

the-life-of-thomas-telford-civil-enginee: Samuel Smiles's life of Thomas Telford, the great civil engineer: bridges, canals, and roads across Britain. crito: Plato's dialogue on obedience to law: Socrates in prison refuses Crito's offer of escape. Short, noble, and profound, it defines the citizen's duty. One of the most moving passages in philosophy. Socrates argues that a just man cannot return injustice for injustice.
majjhima-nikaya-sujato:
Bhikkhu Sujato translated the Majjhima Nikaya, the Middle Discourses of the Buddha, into modern English. The collection holds 152 discourses of medium length from the Pali canon. It forms the second great collection of the Sutta Pitaka.

Many discourses stage conversations with kings, monks, wanderers, and skeptics. Teachings cover meditation, ethics, karma, and the nature of the self. Famous pieces include instructions on mindfulness and the simile of the raft. Sujato's plain English, released freely through SuttaCentral, favors clarity over ornament. The Majjhima is often called the heart of early Buddhism. New readers of the Buddha usually begin somewhere inside this collection.
udana-sujato:
Bhikkhu Sujato translated the Udana, the Heartfelt Sayings of the Buddha, into modern English. The Udana belongs to the Khuddaka Nikaya of the Pali canon. It collects eighty inspired utterances, each told with its story.

A blind-from-birth parable, an elephant, and watching fishermen spark famous sayings. Each short narrative ends in a glad verse outburst from the Buddha. The collection's tone feels spontaneous where other texts feel systematic. Sujato's fresh translation, shared freely through SuttaCentral, keeps that spontaneity alive. English readers meet the Buddha reacting to daily events here. Among the most human and delightful texts of the canon, the Udana rewards casual browsing.
itivuttaka-sujato:
Bhikkhu Sujato translated the Itivuttaka, meaning As It Was Said, into modern English. The collection holds 112 short sayings of the Buddha in the Khuddaka Nikaya. Each saying opens with the formula that names the book.

Teachings on greed, kindness, and heedfulness appear in compact prose and verse. Many sayings pair a prose statement with a verse restatement for memory. Tradition says a laywoman named Khujjuttara preserved these teachings by hearing them. Sujato's plain modern English, released freely, suits the terse originals. The Itivuttaka works as Buddhism's pocket wisdom for daily reflection. Its brevity hides a complete ethical teaching in miniature form here.
khuddakapatha-sujato:
Bhikkhu Sujato translated the Khuddakapatha, the Minor Readings, into modern English. The little book gathers nine short texts from the Khuddaka Nikaya. Novice monks across the Theravada world still learn it by heart.

Refuges, precepts, and blessings make up the beginner's prayer book of Buddhism. The famous Discourse on Goodwill, the Metta Sutta, stands among its nine pieces. Other texts praise the Buddha's virtues and answer a god's questions. Sujato's translation gives the whole set in clear English. Small in size, the Khuddakapatha stays central to daily Buddhist life. Two thousand years of beginners have started exactly here with these readings.
theragatha-sujato:
Bhikkhu Sujato translated the Theragatha, Verses of the Elder Monks, in a complete modern version. The collection holds 264 verse pieces by enlightened monks of early Buddhism. It belongs to the Khuddaka Nikaya of the Pali canon.

Forest hermits, reformed killers, and footsore wanderers sing of peace here. Monks recall fevers, temptations, and the moment of final release. Some verses praise rain, peacocks, and mountain solitude with real beauty. Sujato's complete translation carries every voice across into direct English. An older verse translation by Rhys Davids covers the same ground partially. The Theragatha stands as early Buddhism's great chorus of liberation poetry.
therigatha-sujato:
Bhikkhu Sujato translated the Therigatha, Verses of the Elder Nuns, in a complete modern version. Seventy-three verse pieces by enlightened Buddhist women survive in the collection. It is one of the oldest women's religious texts in the world.

Nuns sing of grief overcome, resolve tested, and joy in freedom. A mother who lost her child and a former courtesan speak plainly. Their poems were composed roughly twenty-five centuries ago in India. Sujato's direct modern English keeps their voices startlingly alive. A 1909 translation by Rhys Davids first introduced the Sisters to English. This complete version lets every nun in the collection be heard.
anguttara-nikaya-sujato:
Bhikkhu Sujato translated the Anguttara Nikaya, the Numbered Discourses, in a complete modern version. The collection is the fourth great book of the Sutta Pitaka. It holds 1,313 discourses arranged in eleven books by number.

Ones come first: one vital quality that changes everything for practice. Twos, threes, and onward climb the ladder to elevens by the end. Three poisons, four noble truths, and five hindrances fit the scheme naturally. The arrangement served monks who memorized the teaching orally for centuries. Sujato's translation makes the vast memory-library easy to walk through. English readers can now browse the whole numbered system freely online.
samyutta-nikaya-sujato:
Bhikkhu Sujato translated the Samyutta Nikaya, the Connected Discourses, in a complete modern version. The collection is the third great book of the Sutta Pitaka. It packs 1,685 discourses into fifty-six linked chapters called samyuttas.

Each chapter gathers teachings on one theme in tight sequence. The aggregates, the senses, and dependent origination receive deep treatment. The noble truths and the path get their own long connected sections. Reasoners prize this collection as the Pali canon's most systematic heart. Sujato's translation opens it fully to English readers for free. Early Buddhism's core doctrines receive their fullest connected statement in these discourses.
doe-osti-3385039-on-transforming-the-spe: Your phone finds itself with satellites, but missiles and aircraft need navigation that never drops out. This paper works through the math of transforming the specific force vector — the accelerations an inertial sensor feels — for ECEF navigation systems. Precise transforms keep dead-reckoning honest when GPS is gone.
nasa-tm-19660001918-the-response-of-magn: Earthquakes shake the ground — and sensitive magnetic instruments feel it. This 1966 NASA report studies the response of magnetic instruments to earthquake waves. The work helped separate real magnetic signals from seismic noise in the data.
nasa-tm-19680006069-evolution-toward-a-s: Space law didn't appear overnight — it grew from decades of debate. This 1968 NASA report traces the evolution toward a space treaty in a historical analysis. The study captured the legal thinking that shaped the rules governing the final frontier.
nasa-tm-19700026244-sensitivity-of-earth: Tiny velocity errors at the orbit's extremes can snowball. This 1970 Apollo report studies the sensitivity of Earth and lunar orbits to velocity changes at periapsis and apoapsis. The analysis quantified how small burns — or mistakes — reshape the trajectory.
nasa-tm-19710012919-contributions-of-the: Space research paid aviation back — this lecture explains how. This 1971 NASA lecture — number 13 in the Space and Aviation series, Session E — covers contributions of the space programme to aviation. The talk traced the technology flowing from rockets to airliners.
